observations.text: SP, due to a delayed and incomplete trim technique during the climb as Wingman, did not maintain A/C control and did not preserve flight parameters within the specified limitations, with the result of an altitude excursion of about 450 feet and an airspeed excursion of about 30 knots, beyond the code 1 limits of 300 feet and 20 knots. The IP directed the pitch and power corrections and flew part of the level off. Further practice in basic A/C control within the formation is required.

SP, due to attention captured by the Leader's aircraft at the expense of the instrument cross-check, did not monitor the A/C state during the descent as Wingman, with the result of an altitude excursion of about 500 feet and an airspeed excursion of about 35 knots, both beyond the code 1 limits of 300 feet and 20 knots. The IP took the controls to re-establish the briefed parameters. The required report to the Leader on the abnormal situation was not made.

SP maintained A/C control within the desired standards for the Training Section, keeping altitude within 280 feet and airspeed within 18 knots through the climb and the level off. Recognition of the developing trend was delayed on two occasions and the corrections followed the IP's verbal prompts. Marginal performance for this block - earlier detection of the deviation trend and prompter trim application are expected to improve.

SP, as Wingman, maintained A/C control and monitored Gs throughout the sortie, holding altitude within 200 feet and airspeed within 15 knots. The deviations that developed during the climb were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention, and trim was applied after each power and configuration change. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP preserved flight parameters within the specified limitations during climb, descent, level off and cruise, holding altitude within 120 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and exit headings within 4 degrees. Trim was applied promptly in every flight phase and G load was kept well inside the 4 G limit, with immediate reports to the Leader on each parameter change. Control of the A/C was accurate, timely and self-sufficient. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the profile with negligible deviations, holding altitude within 50 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and exit headings within 2 degrees while remaining inside the assigned area. Trim was continuously refined, G onset was smooth and positive at all times, and every abnormal indication was reported to the Leader without delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an abrupt pitch and power technique at the level off as Leader, did not preserve flight parameters within the specified limitations and did not respect the Wingman's A/C limitations, with the result of an altitude excursion of about 500 feet and an airspeed excursion of about 30 knots, beyond the code 1 limits of 300 feet and 20 knots. The IP directed the recovery and flew part of the level off to protect the Wingman. Smooth and positive control of the A/C must be re-established before the next event.

SP, due to lack of awareness of the aircraft's position relative to the area boundary, did not keep the formation within the assigned area while leading and did not maintain orientation within the flight area, with the result of an exit heading error of about 20 degrees against the code 1 limit of 10 degrees. The IP directed the turn back inside the working area and re-established the formation's position. Area study and continuous position awareness are required.

SP, due to late and incomplete trim application after each configuration change, did not hold the briefed cruise parameters as Wingman, with the result of altitude deviations reaching 300 feet and airspeed deviations reaching 20 knots, that is the code 1 limits. Recognition of the trend was delayed and the corrections were applied only after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained on the Leader's aircraft, did not report to the Leader that flight parameters had reached their limits, with the result of an exit heading error of 10 degrees and an airspeed excursion of 20 knots, both at the code 1 limits. Both deviations were recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompting.

SP maintained A/C control within the desired standards, keeping altitude within 220 feet, airspeed within 16 knots and exit headings within 8 degrees. Two deviations developed inside the turns but were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter parameter control and earlier trim application are expected to improve.

SP preserved flight parameters within the specified limitations during climb, descent, level off and cruise, holding altitude within 130 feet, airspeed within 9 knots and exit headings within 4 degrees. Trim was applied promptly, radio calls and visual signals preceded every maneuver and configuration change, and the formation was kept inside the assigned area without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew both as Leader and as Wingman with negligible deviations, holding altitude within 60 feet, airspeed within 4 knots and exit headings within 2 degrees, and keeping bank angles inside the limits applicable to the Wingman's position. G load was controlled smoothly and positively well below 4 Gs, trim was continuously maintained, and orientation within the flight area was retained at all times. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to coarse and out-of-trim control inputs during the descent as Leader, did not preserve flight parameters within the specified limitations for the Wingman, with the result of an altitude excursion of about 450 feet and an airspeed excursion of about 35 knots, both beyond the code 1 limits of 300 feet and 20 knots. The IP intervened on the controls to stabilize the formation. Basic A/C control at the required standard was not demonstrated without assistance.

SP, due to overconfidence in the margin available at that airspeed and bank, exceeded the 60 degrees of bank allowed with the Wingman in Route and did not maintain control of the G load within the 4 G limit. The IP took the controls to unload the aircraft and reposition the formation, with an exit heading error of about 25 degrees against the code 1 limit of 10 degrees. Energy awareness and respect for the bank limits applicable to the Wingman's position require further work.

SP, due to a fixed power setting technique carried through the level off, did not preserve airspeed and altitude within the specified limitations as Leader, with the result of deviations reaching 20 knots and 300 feet, that is the code 1 limits. Recognition of the developing trend was delayed and the parameters were restored only after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP, due to workload distribution that left station keeping and navigation display management competing for the same attention, did not hold the assigned cruise parameters, with the result of an exit heading error of 10 degrees and an altitude deviation of 300 feet, both at the code 1 limits. The correction followed only after the IP's verbal prompting and the required report to the Leader was omitted.

SP, due to slightly delayed trim application after the power change, did not hold the briefed cruise parameters precisely, with the result of an altitude deviation of about 200 feet and an airspeed deviation of about 15 knots. Both deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic during the working phase of the sortie, did not maintain the exit heading and the airspeed as briefed, with the result of a heading error of about 8 degrees and an airspeed deviation of about 14 knots. The deviations were self-recognized and corrected promptly, with no IP intervention required.

SP maintained A/C control accurately and preserved flight parameters within the specified limitations, holding altitude within 140 feet, airspeed within 9 knots and exit headings within 5 degrees, that is close to the desired limits. Trim was applied promptly and the formation was kept inside the assigned area. Marginal performance within the desired standards - a wider margin on altitude and heading control inside the turns is expected to improve.

SP maintained A/C control with negligible deviations both as Leader and as Wingman, holding altitude within 50 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and exit headings within 2 degrees throughout climb, descent, level off and cruise. Maneuvers were flown smoothly and within the Wingman's A/C limitations, with all radio calls and visual signals given before each maneuver and configuration change, and G load controlled positively well inside 4 Gs. Orientation within the flight area was retained at all times and the formation was kept fluid with respect to fuel, weather and the flight area. Above end of block MIF achieved.
